candidates: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:482 - `isAccessTokenId` never checks the grant shortcut: it reads the wrong offset and the condition is inverted.. The grant shortcut sits at characters 4–5 of the prefix (`encodedContext.substring(4, 6)` in the decoder). The matcher instead takes `substring(3, 5)`, which for `onrtac` is `ta`. It then returns false when that value *equals* the expected shortcut. The two mistakes together mean that, in practice, any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` passes whatever the grant. The test assertions that replaced `isUUID()` therefore never verify the encoded grant type, and a wrong grant encoding would go unnoticed. Fix: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Also check `items[0].length() == 6` first.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 - The null check meant for `rawTokenId` checks `grantType` again.. `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` a second time. A null `rawTokenId` is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` would then produce an ID like `onrtac:null`. Change the argument to `rawTokenId`.
